title: What makes a muscle grow
summary: Muscles grow from hard sets that put them under high tension. Sets near failure count, failure itself adds little, loading the stretch looks promising, and the pump and soreness are not required.

features: Hard-set rule in the logger (rules.json logger.hardRIR)
Set tags: failure, partials, drop sets, myo-reps (rules.json logger.set_tags)
Swap sheet 'More stretch emphasis' line (rules.json swap_tags)
app_link.explains: Why the app counts hard sets, why a set to failure counts the same as a set at 1-3 RIR, and why some exercises are marked as stretch-biased.

sections.heading: Mechanical tension is the main signal
body: A muscle grows when its fibres produce high force for enough reps. Heavy loads do that from the first rep. Lighter loads get there too, but only near the end of a set, when fatigue forces more and more fibres to work hard.
That is why rep range matters less than effort: sets of 6 or 25 reps can both build muscle if they end close to failure. Heavy sets still build more strength.

points.text: Tension sensed by the muscle fibres is the best-supported trigger for growth. Metabolic stress and muscle damage are less certain contributors.
Light and heavy loads grew muscle about equally when sets were taken to failure; heavy loads gave more strength.
The app's default rep ranges (6-10 for primary lifts, 8-12 for accessories, 10-15 for isolation) are practical choices for steady progress, not growth thresholds.

sections.heading: How close to failure
body: Reps in reserve (RIR) is how many more good reps you could have done. Sets that end closer to failure tend to grow muscle more, but going all the way to failure has not shown a clear extra benefit, and it costs more fatigue.

The app turns this into one rule: a working set counts as a hard set when you log RIR 3 or less, or no RIR at all. A set tagged Failure counts as one hard set, the same as a set at RIR 1-3. There is no failure bonus.

points.text: Across studies, muscle growth rose as sets were stopped closer to failure. Strength gains were similar across a wide range of RIR. The analysis is exploratory, so the exact curve is uncertain.
Training to momentary failure did not produce clearly more growth than stopping a little short of it.
Stopping very far from failure (many reps in reserve) likely counts for less, so the app does not count logged sets above RIR 3 as hard sets.
The cut-off at RIR 3 is a modeling choice. Neither paper defines a threshold; you can change it in settings (0 to 5).
A failure-tagged set gets a hard-set credit of 1.0, the same as any hard set.
The board assumes every planned set will be a hard set. Logging RIR is what lets the app check that afterwards.

sections.heading: Training the stretched position
body: Several studies found more growth when the hardest part of the rep was at a long muscle length, with the muscle stretched: seated rather than lying leg curls, the bottom half of leg extensions and calf raises, and the straight-arm part of preacher curls.

Pooled together, the edge is small and uncertain, and lengthened partials have matched full reps rather than beaten them in trained people. Treat it as a useful tie-breaker when picking exercises, not a rule that overrides effort and volume.

points.text: Seated leg curls (hamstrings at longer length) grew the hamstrings more than lying leg curls.
Partials in the stretched range grew the quads and calves more than partials in the shortened range.
Preacher curls in the straight-arm range grew the elbow flexors more than the bent-arm range.
Across studies, partial vs full range made a small, uncertain difference, with a possible edge for partials at long lengths.
In trained people, lengthened partials grew the arms about as much as full reps did.
Exercises in the app's stretch-biased list show 'More stretch emphasis' in the swap sheet when they replace a less stretch-focused move.

Analytics marks a muscle's stretch share as low, and suggests a stretch-biased exercise, when under 25% of its planned credited sets come from its stretch-biased list. The 25% line is a model, not a measured threshold.
A set tagged Partials (meant as lengthened partials) counts as a full hard set when it is hard; it is left out of PRs because partial reps are not comparable with full reps.

sections.heading: What it isn't
body: A pump, a burn and next-day soreness are things you may feel, not signs that a session worked. Soreness mostly reflects new or unaccustomed work and fades as you adapt, while growth carries on.
Judge sessions by what the app tracks: hard sets per muscle, and loads or reps going up over time.

points.text: Early in a programme, muscle protein synthesis went mostly to repair while damage was high; it lined up with growth only after damage faded. Soreness and damage are not the growth signal.
No good evidence shows that chasing a pump adds growth beyond the hard sets that produce it.
Low-load sets that burn work because they end near failure, not because of the burn itself.

sections.heading: How the app puts it together
body: Each hard set adds its exercise's muscle rating to that muscle's weekly total (1.0 for a main mover, about 0.5 for a helper, ratings under 0.25 count as 0). More hard sets per week tend to give more growth, with diminishing returns, which the weekly targets and the stimulus curve try to reflect.
The details of set counting, targets and the curve are on the 'Set crediting and weekly targets' and 'Volume and frequency' pages.

points.text: More weekly hard sets per muscle went with more growth, with diminishing returns at higher volumes.
Counting indirect sets as a fraction is loosely based on Pelland 2026, where counting indirect sets as half a set fit best. The per-exercise ratings and the 0.25 cut-off are coaching estimates.
In the stimulus curve, effective sets past 10 for one muscle in one session count at 50%. This is a heuristic, not a measured limit.

notes: Most studies are short (5 to 12 weeks), small, and many use untrained people. Results are averages; individuals vary.
The app's numbers (hard-set cut-off, credits, stretch-share flag, session discount) are models built on these findings, marked modeled. Render them from the data files, not from this text.
This page makes no medical claims.
